chunks.l2:
[tal-a24-v01] Now hear the secret final sacrament taught in the Śāmbhava teaching.

[tal-a24-v10] For them it is to be performed here by the ultra-compassionate guru; but no maṇḍala-etc. here — in the cremation-ground rite.

[tal-a24-v02] For all from lower stations up to gurus, clearly: after the aforesaid śaktipāta one should perform the funerary initiation.

[tal-a24-v03] And for followers of the upper teaching whose selves are samaya-struck, the funerary initiation is to be performed by the tattva-knowing guru.

[tal-a24-v04] For him who stumbled through negligence into samaya-conduct faults, the funerary initiation is to be done — so in the venerable Dīkṣottara teaching.

[tal-a24-v05] Whatever was told before in the rite called corpse-uplifting — that entire procedure here, on the corpse-body, he should perform, there on the image.

[tal-a24-v06] This rule told in the Siddhātantra is set forth: what would be last, making that last first and first last.

[tal-a24-v07] Having withdrawn each oblation, the funerary rite is held twofold — but not so for the sādhaka whose samaya is bathed in worship, meditation, and mantra.

[tal-a24-v08] From the body's fall this one is freed, or becomes a sky-rover, dear lady; when the tattva-accomplished teacher has died, wherever it be.

[tal-a24-v09] No funerary rite at all is found for the pure-minded; but those killed by mantra-yoga rites are in hell — they.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C24 atha śrītantrāloke caturviṃśatitamamāhnikam atha śāmbhavaśāsanoditāṃ sarahasyāṃ śṛṇutāntyasaṃskriyām sarveṣāmadharasthānāṃ gurvantānāmapi sphuṭam / śaktipātātpurāproktātkuryādantyeṣṭidīkṣaṇam ūrdhvaśāsanagānāṃ ca samayopahatātmanām / antyeṣṭidīkṣā kartavyā guruṇā tattvavedinā samayācāradoṣeṣu pramādātskhalitasya hi / antyeṣṭidīkṣā kāryeti śrīdīkṣottaraśāsane yatkiṃcitkathitaṃ pūrvaṃ mṛtoddhārābhidhe vidhau / pratimāyāṃ tadevātra sarvaṃ śavatanau caret śrīsiddhātantrakathito vidhireṣa nirūpyate / antimaṃ yadbhavetpūrvaṃ tatkṛtvāntimamādimam saṃhṛtyaikaikamiṣṭiryā sāntyeṣṭirdvitayī matā / pūjādhyānajapāpluṣṭasamaye natu sādhake piṇḍapātādayaṃ muktaḥ khecaro vā bhavetpriye / ācārye tattvasaṃpanne yatra tatra mṛte sati antyeṣṭirnaiva vidyeta śuddhacetasyamūrdhani / mantrayogādibhirye ca māritā narake tu te kāryā teṣāmihāntyeṣṭirguruṇātikṛpālunā / na maṇḍalādikaṃ tvatra bhavecchamāśānike vidhau

chunks.l2:
[tal-a24-v11] Some said even that is to be done in the mortuary: having worshipped the Omnipresent, he should perform the entire nyāsa as before.

[tal-a24-v12] By dissolution-sequence, from the foot to the head-end, just so should he awaken him — with rite, knowledge, and absorption.

[tal-a24-v13] With bindu he should block the tattva, with the śakti-seed pierce; at the nāda-place he should rub, and with the trident strike.

[tal-a24-v14] With what lies inside suṣumnā indeed, with emission again and again he should strike all the kalās; then this bound soul trembles.

[tal-a24-v15] He should raise the left hand — or then join him to the Supreme; without proof, liberation is indeed unbelievable to the deluded.

[tal-a24-v16] For this purpose this is taught — but not as giving what serves liberation; thus said the Supreme Lord in the venerable Kulagahvara teaching.

[tal-a24-v17] The to-be-proved, like liberation, is to be inferred through proofs, since beyond the senses; and in the Dīkṣottara the puryaṣṭaka-class offering is taught.

[tal-a24-v18] Its rite: on the ear-petal lotus, in the middle the god Sadāśiva, the Īśa-Rudra-Hari-Brahman tetrad beginning with the east quarter.

[tal-a24-v19] Having worshipped, hearing and touch, taste, smell, the twofold body, intellect and ego, and mind — to Brahmā and the rest he should offer in order.

[tal-a24-v20] Having made their libation, with a hundred fire-offerings the guide effects this renunciate initiation, purifying the city-of-eight.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kecittadapi kartavyamūcire pretasadmani / pūjayitvā vibhuṃ sarvaṃ nyāsaṃ pūrvavadācaret saṃhārakramayogena caraṇānmūrdhapaścimam / tathaiva bodhayedenaṃ kriyājñānasamādhibhiḥ bindunā rodhayettattvaṃ śaktibījena vedhayet / ghaṭṭayennādadeśe tu triśūlena tu tāḍayet suṣumnāntargatenaiva visargeṇa punaḥ punaḥ / tāḍayeta kalāḥ sarvāḥ kampate@sau tataḥ paśuḥ utkṣipedvāmahastaṃ vā tatastaṃ yojayetpare / pratyayena vinā mokṣo hyaśraddheyo vimohitaiḥ tadarthametaduditaṃ natu mokṣopayogyadaḥ / ityūce parameśaḥ śrīkulagahvaraśāsane sādhyo@numeyo mokṣādiḥ pratyayairyadatīndriyaḥ / dīkṣottare ca puryaṣṭavargārpaṇamihoditam tadvidhiḥ śrutipatre@bje madhye devaṃ sadāśivam / īśarudraharibrahmacatuṣkaṃ prāgdigāditaḥ pūjayitvā śrutisparśau rasaṃ gandhaṃ vapurdvayam / dhyahaṃkṛtī manaśceti brahmādiṣvarpayetkramāt eteṣāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā śatahomena daiśikaḥ / eṣā sāṃnyāsikī dīkṣā puryaṣṭakaviśodhanī

chunks.l2:
[tal-a24-v21] And with the puryaṣṭaka gone, no heaven, hell, and the rest; having done thus, nothing worldly at all is to be done indeed.

[tal-a24-v22] Said in the venerable Mādhavakula: established in the teaching, even for the dead, he should abandon piṇḍa-offerings, water, tears — the worldly.

[tal-a24-v23] Having fully worshipped Śiva, he should perform the wheel-worship according to capacity, in order on the memorial days.

[tal-a24-v24] Thus told is this funerary sacrifice, spoken by the Supreme Lord.
